options.a: Drug name and total amount used per month, reconciled yearly
options.b: Date, client/patient, drug, amount, balance, and responsible personnel
options.c: Date, drug, and dose only, with the running balance tracked by the distributor
options.d: Client name and drug, signed later by the DVM at month end

distractorExplanations.c: The clinic keeps its own running balance, not the distributor, and each entry must also record the client/patient and who handled the drug.
distractorExplanations.a: Monthly totals do not meet DEA rules; each dispensing/administration entry must be logged with a running balance.
distractorExplanations.d: Entries are made at the time of use by the person handling the drug, not batch-signed by the DVM at month end.

options.d: Hyperdynamic septic shock with brick-red membranes

distractorExplanations.d: Hyperdynamic septic shock shows brick-red membranes and a CRT under 1 second, not the normal pink membranes described here.
distractorExplanations.b: Hypovolemic shock gives pale membranes and a CRT longer than 2 seconds, not pink with a quick CRT.
distractorExplanations.c: About 8% dehydration shows tacky membranes and slowed CRT; moist membranes argue against it.
